claims.text: The declared fitted example uses seed7,12 noisy training rows,256 held-out rows and widths1,2,3,6,9,11,12,13,16,24,48. Fullprecision saved least-squares weights are evaluated against the pinned raw matrices; this is fixture evaluation, not fresh training. At noisy widths3,12,16,48, held-out MSE rounds to0.07,5.32,0.68,1.06; the12/16 training residuals round to0.00. Clean evaluates noiseless fitted weights on the same matrices; held-out12/16 errors round to0.00/0.47. All displayed MSE rounds to two decimals; plotted residuals use unrounded values on one width/log-width coordinate axis. One seed does not establish a monotonic benefit from width.

claims.text: At width 12, training error vanishes while held-out error peaks. Width 16 lowers that peak but still loses to width 3. Removing training noise changes this comparison. These are fitted results from one seed, not a promise that adding width improves prediction.
